summary: Created the Fleet Internal CA, issued node2’s TLS certificate, and configured persistent HTTPS on node2:8443. Both nodes trust the CA, and all configuration survived sequential node restarts without changing AlmaLinux 9.6 or kernel 5.14.0-570.12.1.el9_6.
actions_performed: Created the CA and protected its private key on node1.
Generated node2’s private key on node2 and signed its CSR on node1.
Installed Fleet Internal CA as a system trust anchor on both nodes.
Configured and enabled fleet-https.service on node2.
Permanently allowed TCP/8443 through node2’s firewall.
Verified HTTP 200 with successful system TLS validation.
Restarted node1 and node2 sequentially and verified changed boot identities and recovery.

evidence.requirement: Fleet Internal CA creation and node2 certificate issuance
evidence.summary: Shows the CA subject, validated CSR, signed certificate chain, Fleet Internal CA issuer, server-auth usage, and certificate validity.
Both system trust stores identify Fleet Internal CA as an anchor, including after restart.

evidence.requirement: node2 serves trusted HTTPS on port 8443
evidence.summary: The enabled service listens on 8443, the firewall permits it, and node1 receives HTTP 200 with TLS_VERIFY=0 before and after restarts.

evidence.requirement: node2 certificate identity and private-key consistency
evidence.summary: Verifies the certificate chain, matching private key, CN node2, DNS node2 and IP 10.100.204.11 SANs.
Healthy baseline boot ID, acknowledged restart, changed boot ID, and recovered CA artifacts, trust, certificate verification, and HTTPS connectivity.
Healthy baseline boot ID, acknowledged restart, changed boot ID, and recovered HTTPS service, listener, firewall rule, certificates, trust, and cross-node connectivity.
Both nodes remained on AlmaLinux 9.6 and kernel 5.14.0-570.12.1.el9_6 before and after configuration and restart.
